firmware.note: firmware/status serves a minimal envelope until a check has run since boot, then a state-dependent superset (~26 top-level keys, we model 12); the unmodelled remainder is exempted wholesale so canary results do not depend on when the box last ran a check. downgrade_packages/reinstall_packages are now modelled as count gauges (#237). The 26.7 full-inventory keys (all_packages/all_sets) remain a #227 opportunity - deliberately NOT decoded, so raw composite inventories never become per-package metrics (#373 scope). connection/repository/remove_packages/upgrade_sets/download_size were REMOVED from this list on 2026-07-25: #373 models connection/repository as bounded update-check state and remove_packages/upgrade_sets as count gauges, and #380 models download_size as a byte gauge, so they are no longer unmodelled. upgrade_packages[].size is BOX STATE, not drift: core's check.sh builds an ordinary package-upgrade entry as name/repository/current_version/new_version with no size key at all (check.sh:271-281), and emits size only on the synthetic base and kernel entries, each guarded on opnsense-update reporting a non-empty size (check.sh:328-337, 350-359). FirmwareController.php:133 reads it back behind !empty()+is_numeric(), so upstream itself treats it as optional. The field therefore appears only while a BASE OR KERNEL upgrade is pending; a box with only ordinary package upgrades legitimately omits it. Exempting rather than fixing the testbed is safe here because size backs no exported metric - it is parsed into firmware.go's UpgradePackages struct but never copied into FirmwarePackageUpgrade, so the canary blinds us to nothing consumed. PRUNE TRIGGER: if size is ever consumed by a metric, delete this entry and instead hold a pending base/kernel upgrade on the testbed so the path is genuinely covered MINIMAL-ENVELOPE ADDITIONS 2026-07-25 (#373/#380): connection, repository, download_size, remove_packages, upgrade_sets, downgrade_packages and reinstall_packages are ALL state-dependent top-level keys that exist only AFTER a check has been stored. Verified live the same day: the dev box served the full 26-key superset at 18:33, then reverted to the bare 3-key envelope (product/status/status_msg, status=none) after a package operation cleared the stored check - and the canary flagged all seven as Missing. This is BOX STATE, not drift, exactly like the pre-existing entries above. downgrade_packages/reinstall_packages were a latent gap from #237 that only became visible once a run caught the box pre-check. The remove_packages[].* and upgrade_sets[].* prefixes cover the element paths for the same reason. PRUNE TRIGGER: none - this is permanent box state, since a box that has never run a check since boot is a legitimate and reachable state. The exporter handles it by presence-gating on CheckPresent, so no success/state series is fabricated; that gating was live-confirmed by this very reversion.

healthCheck.note: Two unrelated things. (1) The CrashReporter/Firewall/System entries are the legacy pre-25.1 health shape, killed by upstream refactor 1fc5a6335 (2024-12-12). They are ALREADY outside the current+previous support window (26.1 + 25.7), so the trigger has fired — but pruning them is not a ledger edit: the exemptions only exist because the structs do, and deleting the structs drops support for pre-25.1 boxes, which is a product decision rather than canary hygiene. Left in place deliberately; raise an issue if that support should end (#284). (2) 'subsystems' is BOX STATE, not a version prune: SystemController::statusAction() only assigns $response['subsystems'] inside `if ($statuses)`, so a box with no subsystem reporting anything omits the key entirely. Verified 2026-07-17 against upstream source (blob ea83f28a is IDENTICAL on master, stable/26.1 and stable/25.7, unchanged since 2025-01-21) and against a live healthy box. It reappears the moment any subsystem reports, which is why #235 flagged it and #243 did not. metadata.subsystems is NOT populated on any release and is no longer modelled — see #284. knownExtraPaths (#376): the 26.1+ metadata block carries four keys we deliberately do not model. metadata.subsystems is the phantom generation from #284 - upstream never populates it on any release and it was removed from the structs; PRUNE TRIGGER: only if upstream ever populates it with data worth exporting. metadata.translations is GUI i18n text. metadata.System.message/.title are free-form GUI strings; only metadata.System.status is consumed. PRUNE TRIGGER for those three: if a metric ever needs them. Paths are spelled in the STRUCT's casing (System) even though 26.1 serves lowercase 'system' - the validator canonicalizes to the schema spelling on purpose, so the exemption matches every release's casing

interfaceConfig.note: The transceiver block is emitted only for a row ifconfig prints a "plugged:" line for, i.e. a physical port with an SFP cage — legacy_interfaces_details() creates $result[$dev]['sfp'] in that branch alone. The canary box is a virtio-only VM, so NO row carries it and *.sfp is absent wholesale; the prod box's three populated cages serve it and validate normally (verified live 2026-07-25 on both). Box/hardware state, not a version prune — same field, same reason and same prune trigger as the interfacesOverview rows[].sfp entry below: it goes when a canary box with a real SFP cage exists. Note the sfp subtree needs no .* companion here, unlike interfacesOverview: this struct types the block as flexStringMap, a custom unmarshaler, so the schema walker stops at the parent (#371)

interfaces.note: capture timestamp of the interface statistics snapshot; not modelled

interfacesOverview.note: LAGG (laggproto/lagghash/laggstatistics/laggport), bridge (members) and SFP (sfp) fields are hardware/config-dependent — only served by a row that is itself a lagg(4)/bridge(4)/physical-SFP interface. Verified empirically 2026-07-13 (lagg/bridge) and 2026-07-15 (sfp) against the live box: the 26.7-devel VM is virtio-only, so no row carries an sfp block and rows[].sfp is absent wholesale. A box WITH an SFP row (e.g. the prod box's UBNT UF-RJ45-1G) serves the sfp block and validates the sfp.* subtree normally; the exemption only suppresses the box-has-no-SFP case. Box state, not a version prune (#214, #243)

netbirdStatus.note: netbird CLI status --json (client/status.OutputOverview, github.com/netbirdio/netbird) node identity/config/session fields the exporter does not model — an #211 opportunity if a future metric needs them. Separately (not expressible as an exemption here): the daemon-down state serves a bare `[]` instead of this object (verified live 2026-07-13); a canary run that catches the box in that state will report a top-level Mismatch for this endpoint — that is the documented daemon-down fallback (see opnsense/netbird.go), not drift. knownExtraPaths (#376): the nine per-peer fields netbirdPeerDetail deliberately does not model, confirmed against a live enrolled capture 2026-07-25 (16 keys served, 7 modelled). Several are peer identities/addresses and must stay unmodelled unless a metric genuinely needs them - an #211 opportunity, not drift. PRUNE TRIGGER: delete an entry when its field is modelled. Do NOT model lastStatusUpdate casually: its zero value renders as 0000-12-31T23:58:45-00:01, which time.Time.IsZero() does not catch. SEPARATELY, sessionExpiresAt in knownExtraTopKeys above is PROSPECTIVE, NEVER OBSERVED: the packaged netbird (0.74.4, the current OPNsense ceiling) does not emit it - the field first appears in netbird v0.75.0, and even then only for SSO-enrolled peers, which the os-netbird plugin cannot create (it enrols by setup key only). #379 was closed won't-do on that basis 2026-07-25. The entry is harmless (an exemption only suppresses a key that is actually present) and is kept so a future 0.75.0+ package does not trip the canary. PRUNE TRIGGER: delete if the field is ever modelled

nginxVts.note: vts module identity and current-time snapshot; not modelled. loadMsec IS modelled (config_load_timestamp_seconds, #200) and removed from this list. cacheZones is BOX STATE: nginx-module-vts writes the key, calls display_set_cache(), then rewinds the buffer wholesale if nothing was written (display_json.c `s = buf; ...; if (s == buf) { buf = o; }`), so the key vanishes when the vts shared memory holds no cache node — and that shm resets on every nginx reload. The testbed HAS a cache configured (settings/get shows cache_path /var/nginx/cache/heavy) but has served nothing through it. Verified live 2026-07-17 on the 26.7-devel VM; the upstream #define for "cacheZones" is still present on vozlt/nginx-module-vts master. Prune once the testbed serves traffic through a proxy_cache location (#271)
